releases.title: Growth focus includes employment applications
Building permits follow the planning approval; alterations aren't units
notes: A permit issued well before the site's first site plan / subdivision / zoning file (completed more than a year before it, or issued more than 3 years before it) was for what stood there before: it no longer sets the phase or counts toward the build-out. Shortly-earlier permits still count and are flagged (an earlier phase whose site plan isn't published); Mississauga "PDOX TRANSFER FILE" site plans are dated by their original file number.

Alteration permits count units only when they create one (a second suite): balcony repairs or fan-coil replacements listing a building's existing units no longer add homes. Second suites are new homes but don't set a site plan's phase.
Phase rules version 5.

releases.title: Only permits for the site's buildings set its phase
notes: permitRole(): units / res (dwelling building, units not stated) / nonres / servicing / none. Signs (Brampton "Permanent", "Class A-Mobile"), entrances, doors, windows, equipment, sales pavilions, temporary structures, additions and demolitions don't set a site's phase; servicing and shoring permits stay on the site but don't either. On a residential site only permits that build homes count.
Sites made only of such permits are not developments (4,136 permits set aside; the audit reports them).
Minor / limited / express site plans don't approve the building.
A site plan that only reads "Closed" counts as approved only when a building permit was issued after it.
Milestones and the status line use the site's building files only.
Phase rules version 4.

releases.title: Registered subdivisions count as Approved; demolition permits don't set the phase
notes: A plan of subdivision shown as registered counts as the site's approval (houses go from registration to permits without a site plan), unless a newer rezoning on the site is still in review.
Demolition permits (HOUSDEMO / DEMO) no longer set a site's phase or start a redevelopment cycle, unless the site has nothing else.
Phase rules version 3 (re-read, not counted as weekly moves).

releases.title: Approved means site plan approved; jobs in growth
notes: A site is Approved only when a site plan is approved. Zoning / official plan / subdivision / condominium approval keeps it under review, shown as "Zoning approved · site plan pending".
A site plan approved before a newer rezoning still in review no longer counts (it was for an earlier proposal).
Brampton legacy site plans ("Transferred", 1980s-2000s, no dates) don't count for a current proposal; a site with only legacy files is completed.
Committed capacity follows: approved unbuilt units drop from ~47,700 to ~5,800; 585 legacy-only sites leave Active applications.
history.json records a rules change as a re-read, not as phase moves.
Growth tab and area selection show jobs added on development sites for built, approved and proposed, with a jobs bar.
